name: Christ Church, Rawalpindi
assumptions: The entrance is the west end although the dossier heading is 90: heading only records the long axis, so the kit front (+Y) is the chancel end; the geometry is placed by coordinates, not by that label.
No height is published. Wall, ridge, pinnacle and bellcote heights come from a 1.9 m door width on the Dawn front (about 38 px per metre) and two south-west views; expect errors of about a metre.
West wing, aisles and nave widths follow the aerial and photos (nave plus aisles 13.8 m); OSM traces the west arm as one 11.6 m strip, so the aisles overhang the OSM ring by about one metre.
Nave gable and aisle west walls are set flush at 5.7 m behind the west face, read from the aerial, whose parallax is about 0.18 m of eastward lean per metre of height.
Six nave bays counted from the clerestory windows in both south-west photos; the far bays are partly hidden by trees. The north side is mirrored from the south.

Transept end walls and all east-facing and north-facing elevations were not photographed: two large windows and an oculus per gable, and the same two-window side walls, are the plainest repeat of the seen west walls.

Chancel side and east windows (three each) are assumed; the dossier only says the chancel has stained glass. Chancel eaves and ridge are estimates. Its centre sits 1.8 m south of the nave axis because both OSM and the aerial show that.
North-east vestry block seen on the aerial only: position, size and low hipped roof are the plainest form.
Colours are sampled from the December 2025 Dawn photos (bare brick, grey dressings), which differ from the older cream and red-painted views.

Chapel position is the red-roofed building on the aerial, corrected for the same image shift as the church; not confirmed by a source. Its door side and hipped form come from one Dawn photo; the side away from it is mirrored.

The lawn cross stands by the chapel at an estimated position, and its height is estimated from the photo. The mean-sea-level stone, the compound railing and the forecourt beyond a 10 m paved strip are left out.
